findings.summary: In the cli test loop, the base_of closure compares the path to entry.mirror exactly, so for the glob entry the base is never returned.
findings.evidence: `let base_of = |p: &str| base.clone().filter(|_| p == entry.mirror);` For PromptStructure, check_entry asks for the base of `crates/demo/prompts/reader.md`, which never equals `crates/*/prompts/*.md`. The closure returns None, which the plan says gives no finding, so the drifted fixture passes and the `a drifted fixture passes` assertion fails. Step 7 changes only the drift assertions. Fix: In step 7, also change both base_of closures to `filter(|_| entry.covers(p))`, or return the base keyed by the concrete fixture path.

findings.summary: Rules (a) and (b) both match the y8kr shape, so one joined line can give two findings, but the test expects exactly one.
findings.evidence: In `- acceptance_criteria: ... suffice.- deliverables: every path`, the base head `- deliverables:` sits mid-line after `.` (rule a), and the line is a list item with a glued `- ` followed by `deliverables:` (rule b). The plan does not say findings are merged. Fix: State in step 4 that findings are merged so each new line gives at most one finding (for example, rule (b) is skipped for a line rule (a) already flagged), or loosen the assertion to at least one finding naming the bullet.

findings.summary: A new prompt file with no base is never checked, although rule (b) needs no base text.
findings.evidence: Rule (b) judges only the new line: a list item holding a second marker followed by an item head. Skipping files with no base means a new role's prompt with joined bullets reaches the verifier. That is part of the class, and decision 2 exists because roles are added over time. Fix: When the base is missing, treat every line as new and run rule (b) alone (rule a needs base heads). Add one test with a new prompt file.

findings.summary: For items without a colon, the head is a fixed 24-character prefix, which is a heuristic length.
findings.evidence: A base item whose first 24 characters are a common phrase could match quoted prose. The guard on the preceding character in decision 4 limits this, and the tests pin a quoted head. Fix: Optionally require the head to end on a word boundary, or document the 24/8 constants in a comment next to the tests that pin them.

summary: I checked the plan against the code using Read and Grep. It fixes the cause where it starts: the mirror registry in crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs gets new rules, and those rules run at the producer step through mirror_drift_in (producer.rs:75 → check_all at line 85) with no new call site. Every named location exists: REGISTRY (lines 96-121), BaseFn (124), append_only_problem (213), glob_matches/segment_matches (609/619), watches (650), check_entry (681), check_all (737), check_log in decisions.rs (218-266), and the run/tests.rs harness (athena_source_repo 2462, fixing_on_send_back 2479, mirror_job 2501). The glob `crates/*/prompts/*.md` matches all 10 prompt files on disk. D161 is the last entry, so the next is D162. The demonstrations go through production entry points: check_entry and check_all with the REGISTRY entry, plus the full producer loop through mirror_drift_in. Each would fail without the new behavior, and the tests assert on the finding text. The plan answers the earlier rounds' false-positive concern by requiring an item head after a second marker and a guard on the character before a matched head; the tests pin both the real failing shapes and ordinary prose. The dependents list matches what Grep finds for readers of REGISTRY, Rule, Drift.mirror and check_all: the cli mirrors test, send_back.rs, producer.rs line 464 (prints only d.mirror), the decisions.rs guard and the backtest. Athena's three scope findings are explained in decision 10: each extra file is needed for compilation, for the producer-step test harness, or for having a single log parser. What remains are small gaps the producer would hit and fix while testing.
